name: Telegram
hint: polls Telegram, no public URL needed

env.name: TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN
env.comment: the token BotFather gives you

steps: Open Telegram and message @BotFather.
Send /newbot and follow the prompts to name your bot.
Copy the token BotFather returns into TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN in .env.
Run bxAgents serve, then send your bot a message.

name: Slack
hint: Socket Mode, no public URL needed

env.name: SLACK_BOT_TOKEN
env.comment: Bot User OAuth Token (xoxb-...)

env.name: SLACK_APP_TOKEN
env.comment: App-Level Token (xapp-...) for Socket Mode

steps: Create an app at https://api.slack.com/apps.
Turn on Socket Mode and make an App-Level Token. Put it in SLACK_APP_TOKEN.
Add the bot scopes you need (at least chat:write), install the app to your workspace, and put the Bot User OAuth Token in SLACK_BOT_TOKEN.
Subscribe to the message events your bot should see, then run bxAgents serve and message the bot.

name: Discord
hint: persistent connection, no public URL needed

env.name: DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN
env.comment: the bot token from the Discord developer portal

steps: Create an application and a bot at https://discord.com/developers/applications.
Copy the bot token into DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN in .env.
Turn on the Message Content privileged intent for the bot, or it cannot read messages.
Invite the bot to your server, run bxAgents serve and message it.

name: WhatsApp (Business Cloud API)
hint: Meta calls your server: needs a public https URL

env.name: WHATSAPP_ACCESS_TOKEN
env.comment: Graph API access token

env.name: WHATSAPP_PHONE_NUMBER_ID
env.comment: the WhatsApp Business phone number ID

env.name: WHATSAPP_APP_SECRET
env.comment: the Meta app secret, used to verify inbound webhooks

env.name: WHATSAPP_VERIFY_TOKEN
env.comment: any secret string you choose; Meta echoes it back during setup

steps: Create a Meta app with the WhatsApp product at https://developers.facebook.com/apps and add a business phone number.
Fill in the four WHATSAPP_ values in .env. The verify token is a string you make up.
Deploy so your agent has a public https address. Meta cannot reach localhost.
In the Meta app's WhatsApp configuration, set the callback URL to https://<your-host>/webhooks/whatsapp-cloud and the verify token to your WHATSAPP_VERIFY_TOKEN, then subscribe to the messages field.
Personal WhatsApp accounts are not supported; this uses the official Business Cloud API only.

name: Microsoft Teams
hint: Bot Framework: needs a public https URL

env.name: TEAMS_APP_ID
env.comment: the bot's Microsoft App ID

env.name: TEAMS_APP_PASSWORD
env.comment: the bot's client secret

steps: Register an Azure Bot and note its Microsoft App ID and a client secret. Put them in TEAMS_APP_ID and TEAMS_APP_PASSWORD.
Deploy so your agent has a public https address.
Set the bot's messaging endpoint to https://<your-host>/webhooks/teams.
Add the Teams channel to the bot and message it. Only one-to-one chats are supported.

name: SMS (Twilio)
hint: Twilio calls your server: needs a public https URL

env.name: TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID
env.comment: Account SID from the Twilio console

env.name: TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN
env.comment: Auth token; it also signs inbound webhooks

env.name: TWILIO_FROM_NUMBER
env.comment: your Twilio number in E.164 form, for example +15551234567

steps: Get a phone number in the Twilio console and copy your Account SID and Auth Token into .env.
Put the number in TWILIO_FROM_NUMBER, in E.164 form.
Deploy so your agent has a public https address.
Set the number's incoming-message webhook to https://<your-host>/webhooks/twilio with the POST method.
Behind a proxy or tunnel, set publicUrl in gateways/twilio.bx to the exact address Twilio calls, or signature checks will fail.

name: GitHub comments
hint: answers when @mentioned: needs a public https URL

env.name: GITHUB_TOKEN
env.comment: a personal access token with repo issues and pull request write access

env.name: GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET
env.comment: any secret string you choose

env.name: GITHUB_BOT_NAME
env.comment: the bot account's GitHub login

steps: Create a bot account (or use your own) and a personal access token. Put it in GITHUB_TOKEN and the account's login in GITHUB_BOT_NAME.
Make up a secret and put it in GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET.
Deploy so your agent has a public https address.
In the repository's settings add a webhook to https://<your-host>/webhooks/github with the same secret, sending issue comment and pull request review comment events.
Comment @<bot name> on an issue or pull request to talk to the agent.

name: Email
hint: reads an IMAP inbox, replies by SMTP

env.name: IMAP_HOST
env.comment: the IMAP server, for example imap.example.com

env.name: IMAP_USERNAME
env.comment: the mailbox login

env.name: IMAP_PASSWORD
env.comment: the mailbox password or app password

env.name: EMAIL_FROM_ADDRESS
env.comment: the address replies are sent from

steps: Create a mailbox for the agent and fill in the four values in .env. Many providers need an app password for IMAP.
Outbound mail goes through BoxLang's mail settings, so configure your SMTP server as described in the Email gateway page.
The inbox is checked about once a minute. Replies are threaded by message headers.

name: Signal
hint: needs signal-cli running on this machine

env.name: SIGNAL_ACCOUNT
env.comment: the phone number registered with signal-cli, in E.164 form

steps: Install signal-cli and register or link it to a Signal account. This is a manual, one-time step.
Start its HTTP daemon: signal-cli daemon --http. The gateway expects it at http://127.0.0.1:8080.
Put the account's phone number in SIGNAL_ACCOUNT, in E.164 form.
Run bxAgents serve and message that number. Direct messages only.
